name: Ixil

new_statements.quote: Both systems consist of quantity-insensitive syllabic trochees within the metrical word. [...] For most speakers, trochees are built from left to right within the metrical word, with primary stress on the initial syllable, and every other syllable to its right receiving secondary stress. In this system, the first syllable of the root is always the most prominent. This is referred to as Stress System A, which is considered to be the primary system for Chajul Ixil. [...] For those speakers, stress patterns are better described as having trochees built from right to left within the metrical word, with primary stress falling on the penultimate syllable

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog codes Ixil as weight-sensitive after Ayres 1991 (Chajul: final stress if the last vowel is long or the word ends in CC, else penultimate; Nebaj simpler). Adell 2019 states explicitly that Chajul stress is quantity-INSENSITIVE and, for most speakers, root-initial (antepenultimate in trisyllables), with penultimate stress only for a minority of speakers (and Nebaj). Adell also supplies the mechanism behind Ayres's rules: the surface prominence on a final long vowel or on the penult that Ayres reports is the declarative boundary H tone on the penultimate mora, which overrides lexical stress clause-finally (§2.5.4), so Ayres's rules describe the clause-final surface pattern, not lex…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Chajul Ixil: quantity-insensitive syllabic trochees over the metrical word (= the word minus the extrametrical Set A ergative/possessive prefixes). Stress System A (most speakers, 'the primary system'): left-to-right trochees, primary stress on the first syllable of the root, e.g. /ootzaqi-mal/ [ˈʔoː.tsa.ˌχĩ.mal̥], /i-vatz-i-b'al/ [i.ˈva.tsi.ˌɓal]. Stress System B (a minority, older men; also the Nebaj pattern): right-to-left trochees, primary stress on the penultimate syllable, e.g. [ˌʔoː.tsa.ˈχĩ.mal̥]. Phonetic correlates: higher pitch and intensity. In clause-final position a declarative boundary H tone on the penultimate mora overrides lexical stress, so a final long vowel surfaces as prominent (/'ixvaak/ phrase-final stress on the ultima) and a three-syllable System-A word looks penult-stressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Yes: every other syllable to the right of the primary (System A, degenerate final feet permitted, so a lone third syllable takes secondary stress: [ˈʔoː.tsa.ˌχil̥]) or to the left of the primary (System B, no degenerate feet: [ʔoː.ˈtsa.χil̥]).
new_statements.exceptions: Set A markers are extrametrical and cannot bear stress (p. 178); proclitic groups outside the metrical word get a separate right-to-left 'intonational accent' (§2.5.3); the declarative boundary tone (H on the penultimate mora, L on the ultima) overrides primary stress clause-finally, attracting main stress to the penult syllable or to a final long-vowel syllable (pp. 200-201; Lengyel 1980 'syntactic stress'); inter-speaker variation between Systems A and B, only distinguishable in 3-4-syllable words in non-clause-final position (p. 192); fn. 36 p. 181: 'Synchronically, syllable weight does not play a prominent role in the prosody of Chajul Ixil. Stress patterns, for instance, are not sensitive to syllable weight.'
new_statements.identity_note: Adell 2019 describes the Chajul dialect of Ixil (San Gaspar Chajul, El Quiché, Guatemala) only; he states that his minority Stress System B (penultimate) 'also describes the Nebaj system of lexical stress' (p. 192) but gives no Nebaj or Cotzal data. The catalog record (Ayres 1991) gives separate rule sets for Chajul (1-4A) and Nebaj (1-4B). Elliott 1960 (dialect not established, SIL work; likely Nebaj) was not obtained.

readall_conflicts: One disagreement, between the catalog source and the only work opened here. Ayres 1991 (catalog record, classification weight) gives Chajul stress as weight-sensitive: final if the last vowel is long or the word ends in two consonants, otherwise penultimate. Adell 2019 (607-page instrumental study of Chajul, pitch and intensity tracks) states that both Chajul stress systems are 'quantity-insensitive syllabic trochees within the metrical word', that for most speakers primary stress falls on the first syllable of the root (System A) with penultimate stress only for a minority of older speakers (System B, which he says is also the Nebaj system), and in fn. 36 p. 181 that 'Stress patterns.. are not sensitive to syllable weight'. Adell reconciles the two: a declarative boundary H tone sits on the penultimate MORA and overrides lexical stress clause-finally, which puts surface prominence on a final long vowel (bimoraic) and on the penult syllable otherwise, exactly the pattern Ayres wrote down as lexical weight-sensitive rules. So the Ayres rules describe clause-final surface prominence, not word stress. Elliott 1960 could not be opened and contributes nothing.

audit.recode_to: Chajul Ixil lexical stress = quantity-INSENSITIVE syllabic trochees (Adell 2019 sec. 2.5.2): Stress System A (most speakers, 'the primary system'): left-to-right trochees, primary stress on the root-initial syllable of the metrical word (Set A prefixes extrametrical), secondary on alternate syllables to the right; Stress System B (minority, older men; per Adell also the Nebaj lexical system): right-to-left trochees, primary stress on the penult. kind -> not 'weight' (root-initial/left edge for System A ~ penult for System B; what counts as heavy: none); the CVV-final 'final stress' of Ayres 1991 rules 2/4/7 is Adell's declarative BOUNDARY TONE (H on the penultimate mora of the intonational phrase, long V bimoraic, CVC/CV'C monomoraic), domain phrase, which overrides lexical stress in phrase-final = citation forms. At minimum add Adell 2019 to 'contra' with a caution and let the compilers rule between (a) reclassify as quantity-insensitive trochaic (initial~penult by speaker) with the mora-counting boundary tone noted as phrasal, or (b) keep Ayres's surface citation-form generalisation but re-label domain phrase and evidence as contested. Nebaj the secondary-stress rule (Ayres: any final C -> final stress) is also contradicted by Adell's aside (Nebaj = System B penult) and should carry a caution.
